paper.title: Fast Rate Learning in Stochastic First Price Bidding

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic first-price bidding with known bid distribution F
unmapped: repeated first-price auction: bid b in [0,1], utility U(b)=(v-b)F(b)
censored feedback: value V_t observed only when the bid wins (M_t <= B_t)
the learner knows the CDF F of the opponents' maximal bid
settings.definition_quote: First, the bidder submits her bid $B_t$ for the item that is of unknown value $V_t$. The other players submit their bids, the maximum of which is called $M_t$. If $M_t\leq B_t$ (which includes the case of ties), the bidder observes and receives $V_t$ and pays $B_t$. If $B_t< M_t$, the bidder loses the auction and does not observe $V_t$. ... In Section~\ref{sec:known_F}, we will first assume that $F$ is known to the learner.

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic first-price bidding with unknown bid distribution F (M_t observed)
unmapped: repeated first-price auction: bid b in [0,1], utility U(b)=(v-b)F(b)
censored feedback: value V_t observed only when the bid wins; opponents' maximal bid M_t observed every round
F unknown, must be estimated from observed M_t
settings.definition_quote: We treat the case, in Section~\ref{sec:unknown_F}, where the CDF $F$ of the opponents' maximal bid is initially unknown to the learner, assuming that the maximal bid $M_t$ is observed for each auction.

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic first-price bidding, Bernoulli values, known F (lower bound)
unmapped: repeated first-price auction with censored value feedback
the learner knows the CDF F of the opponents' maximal bid (and observes M_t)
settings.definition_quote: Consider all environments where $V_t$ follows a Bernoulli distribution with expectation $v$ and $F$ satisfies Assumption \ref{ass:pseudo-mhr} ...

symbols.F_bstar: F(b^*_{v,F}), probability of winning at the optimal bid
symbols.gamma_ucb: confidence-bonus parameter gamma of the algorithm

conditions: values V_t i.i.d. in [0,1], M_t i.i.d. with CDF F independent of V_t

source.label: th:FPUCBID_general
source.quote: When $\gamma>1$, the regret of UCBid1 is upper-bounded as $$R_T^{v,F} \leq\frac{ \sqrt {2 \gamma}}{F(b^*_{v,F})} \sqrt{T \log T}  + O(\log T)\;.$$

results.notes: Leading term exact plus O(log T) remainder; recorded with O notation. Appendix restates as (1/F(b*)) sqrt(gamma log T)(sqrt T+1)+O(1). Algorithm requires a line search per step.

symbols.lambda_F: upper bound on derivative of phi_F(b)=b+F(b)/f(b) near b*
symbols.C_f: upper bound on density f near b*
symbols.c_f: lower bound on density f near b*

conditions: Assumption 1: F continuously differentiable and strictly log-concave
Assumption 2: c_f < f(b) < C_f on [b*-Delta, b*+Delta] and phi_F' <= lambda on [b*, b*+Delta]

source.label: th:FPUCBID_pseudo_mhr
source.quote: If   $F$ satisfies Assumption \ref{ass:pseudo-mhr} and \ref{ass:lambda_pseudo-mhr}, then, for any $\gamma>1$, $$ R_T^{v,F}\leq  \frac{2\gamma \lambda C_f^2}{F(b^*_{v,F}) c_f}\log^2(T)  + O(\log T) .$$

symbols.c_f: lower bound on density f on [0,1]

conditions: F satisfies Assumption 1, phi' <= lambda, and 0<c_f<f(b)<C_f for all b in [0,1]
strategy is consistent: R_T <= O(T^a) for all a>0 on all such environments
strategy overbids with high probability: exists gamma>0 with P(B_t < b*) < t^{-gamma}

source.label: th:parametric_lower_bound
source.quote: Consider all environments where $V_t$ follows a Bernoulli distribution with expectation $v$ and $F$ satisfies Assumption \ref{ass:pseudo-mhr} and is such that $\phi' \leq \lambda$, and there exists $c_f$ and $C_f$ such that $0<c_f<f(b)<C_f, ~ \forall b \in [0,1]$. If a strategy is such that, for all such environments, $R_T^{v,F}\leq O(T^{a})$, for all $a>0$, and there exists $\gamma >0$ such that $\Po(B_t< b^*)<t^{-\gamma}$, then this strategy must satisfy: ...

results.notes: Restricted to consistent strategies that overbid w.h.p. (optimistic strategies).

conditions: max over v in [0,1] and all CDFs F on [0,1]
holds whether or not the strategy knows F
hard instances use Bernoulli values and discrete F

source.label: th:lower_bound_gen
source.quote: Let $\mathcal{C}$ denote the class of cumulative distribution functions on $[0,1]$. Any strategy, whether it assumes knowledge of $F$ or not, must satisfy \liminf_{T \rightarrow \infty} \frac{\max_{v \in [0,1], F \in \mathcal{C}}R_T^{v,F}}{\sqrt{T}} \geq   \frac{1}{64},

results.notes: Paper says this corresponds to Theorem 6 of Han et al. (2020) and reproves it for completeness; marked not new and also listed in cited_results.

source.label: th:UCBid1+_gen
source.quote: UCBid1+ incurs a regret bounded by $$R_T^{v,F} \leq 12 \sqrt{\frac{\gamma v}{U_{v,F}(b^*_{v,F})}}  \sqrt{T \log T}   + O(\log T), $$ provided that $\gamma>2$.

results.notes: Appendix version gives 12 sqrt(gamma alpha/F(b*)) sqrt(T log T) with alpha=v/(v-b*), equal to main form; second appendix line writes (1/U(b*)) sqrt(v gamma), inconsistent. Recorded main-text form. Per-round cost grows with t (quadratic total), still polynomial.

conditions: Assumption 1: F continuously differentiable and strictly log-concave
Assumption 2: c_f < f < C_f near b* and phi_F' <= lambda on [b*, b*+Delta]

source.label: th:fast_rate
source.quote: If $F$ satisfies Assumptions \ref{ass:pseudo-mhr} and \ref{ass:lambda_pseudo-mhr}, UCBid1+ incurs a regret bounded by $$R_T^{v,F} \leq O\big(T^{1/3+\epsilon}\big), $$ for any $\epsilon>0$, provided that $\gamma>2$.

results.notes: Constants depend on epsilon and instance.

conditions: Assumption 1: F continuously differentiable and strictly log-concave
Assumption 2: c_f < f < C_f near b* and phi_F' <= lambda on [b*, b*+Delta]
tuning: gamma > 2 (as used in the proof via event E)
results.notes: Intermediate result (appendix) superseded by Theorem th:fast_rate; gamma condition not in statement but used in proof.

source.label: th:optiBID
source.quote: O-UCBid1 incurs a regret bounded by $$R_T \leq\frac{4 \sqrt 2}{F(b^*)} \sqrt{ \gamma \log T} (\sqrt{T}+1) + O(1).$$

results.notes: Leading term plus O(1). gamma>1 stated in proof and main text.
